proposed_induced: Acknowledges the patient's pregnancy and reassures that routine self-skin checks and dermatology visits are safe during pregnancy.

Notes that hormonal changes during pregnancy can cause benign skin changes (e.g., melasma, spider angiomas, darkening of existing moles) and advises distinguishing these from true ABCDE warning signs.

Advises avoiding pregnancy-unsafe topical treatments (e.g., retinoids, high-concentration hydroquinone, oral isotretinoin) and recommends consulting an OB or dermatologist before starting any new skin medications.
Recommends informing the dermatologist about the pregnancy prior to any in-person visit to ensure pregnancy-safe evaluation and treatment planning.
